claims: C1 the GOOD response to a medical question explains possible causes of the symptom rather than giving a single diagnosis
C2 the GOOD response suggests a practical precaution (standing up slowly) and advises consulting a doctor for severe or frequent symptoms
C3 the BAD response is a definitive diagnosis and is therefore the negative example of the avoid-regulated-advice rule

concepts.name: avoid_regulated_advice_rule
concepts.gloss: R is subject to the rule that the assistant should equip users with information without providing definitive regulated advice and should include a disclaimer

concepts.name: medical_question
concepts.gloss: Q is a user question asking for a diagnosis or medical explanation of a symptom
concepts.inference: the example is introduced as a medical question, so the class must exist for the example to be about

concepts.name: explains_possible_causes
concepts.gloss: response R explains possible causes of the condition raised in question Q rather than asserting a single cause

concepts.name: gives_definitive_diagnosis
concepts.gloss: response R states a single definitive diagnosis for the condition raised in question Q

concepts.name: advises_doctor_consultation
concepts.gloss: response R advises consulting a doctor for severe, frequent, or otherwise concerning symptoms

concepts.name: suggests_precaution
concepts.gloss: response R suggests a practical precaution (such as standing up slowly) that may prevent the symptom

concepts.name: answers_question
concepts.inference: the example pairs each response with the user question it answers

ontology.gloss: R is the GOOD response in the medical-question example
ontology.body: explains_possible_causes(R, Q), suggests_precaution(R, Q), advises_doctor_consultation(R, Q), answers_question(R, Q)

ontology.gloss: R is the BAD response in the medical-question example
